title: Rationality of a normal birational local extension of a regular surface ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative excellent regular local domain of dimension $2$ [def-exc-excellent-ring] [def-weil-regular-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $R\subset B$ be an injective local homomorphism of local domains inducing an equality of fraction fields, with $B$ normal and of dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Assume $B$ is essentially of finite type over $R$: it is a localization of a finitely generated $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then, for every integral normal scheme $Z$ and proper morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ inducing an isomorphism of function fields, one has $H^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=0$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-sc-function-field] [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. The group here is ordinary Zariski sheaf cohomology of the additive structure sheaf.

source.place: Tags 0B4Q, resolve-lemma-regular-rational, and 0BG0, resolve-lemma-rational-propagates; rational singularity is the vanishing condition of Tag 0B4N, resolve-definition-reduce-to-rational. Excellence ensures the Nagata hypotheses.

proof.text: By the definition of excellence, $R$ is quasi-excellent (and Noetherian). Apply [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata] to this quasi-excellent ring: $R$ is Nagata. Thus the given regular local ring $R$ has the Nagata and dimension-$2$ hypotheses needed for the regular-surface rationality theorem.

Apply [lem-per-regular-surface-rational] to $R$, using regular locality and dimension $2$ from the hypotheses and the Nagata property from Step 1. It follows that $R$ defines a rational singularity. This is the full predicate of [def-per-rational-surface-singularity], whose domain consists of Noetherian normal Nagata local domains of dimension $2$; in particular the normality condition on the base ring for propagation is included. We use the regular-surface theorem as stated, without extracting any additional assertion from its proof.

Apply [lem-per-rational-singularity-birational-propagation] with its rings $(R,S)$ equal to $(R,B)$. Its base ring is a normal Nagata local domain of dimension $2$ defining a rational singularity by Steps 1 and 2. The inclusion is an injective local extension of domains with the same fraction field by hypothesis. The remaining assumptions on $S$ are exactly the given normality, local-domain property, dimension $2$, and essential finite type of $B$. Therefore $B$ defines a rational singularity.

Let $Z$ and $g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be arbitrary as in the conclusion. They satisfy precisely the normal-modification convention in [def-per-rational-surface-singularity]: $g$ is proper, $Z$ is integral and normal, and $g$ induces an isomorphism of function fields. The defining universal vanishing for the rational singularity $B$ from Step 3, evaluated at $(Z,g)$, gives $H^1(Z_{\rm Zar},\mathcal O_Z)=0$. By [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], this is the ordinary Zariski cohomology of the additive structure sheaf specified in the statement. Since $(Z,g)$ was arbitrary, this proves every asserted vanishing.
